brief.todays_call: The dollar runway is narrowing from both ends. July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while Brent pressed to $94.09, $14.09 above the $80 FY27 line, lifting the import bill the earned-dollar side must cover. Reserves last printed $36.42bn on 31 Jul, cover 6.28mo, the August refresh three weeks overdue; exports hold $4.03bn, the taka firm at 122.07. Both inflow engines are flat as the oil claim widens. The book stays defensive on the peg — long reserve visibility, watching the refresh over the daily spot.

sections.verdict: Book frozen — reform floated, capital cushion still gone.
sections.analysis: The banking book is unchanged and the freeze is still the story: NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 2026 print, system CAR 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither number moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates the headline. What moves is the scaffolding around it: BB has unveiled loan-recovery mediation and an ADR track, and the sell-side is running 'how the sector stabilised' copy. All of it repairs the tail; none of it restarts the engine. Private credit sits at 4.98% — liquidity is not the constraint, creditworthy demand is. Dispersion stays the trade: own the private compounders, fade the SCB paper the resolution regime tests first.

sections.verdict: Brent presses to $94.09 — $14.09 over the FY27 line.
sections.analysis: Crude is the day's cleanest one-way trade, with the widest reach into the book. Brent broke $90 and has pressed to $94.09, WTI $86.85 — the level that capped it now sits below, and the move is extending rather than fading toward the $80 FY27 assumption it is now $14.09 above. The transmission into Bangladesh is direct and compounding: each dollar re-widens an import bill a $1.77bn trade gap already strains, and lifts a fuel-subsidy claim the FY27 budget provisioned at $80. It also threatens the inflation turn the MPC awaits — non-food CPI already prints 9.61% on the Jun read, energy cost-push not yet in the base. Crude is now the swing variable across FX, fiscal and macro at once — position for a wider import bill and a later, shallower easing path if Brent holds above $90 into the next prints.

chart_read.context: Up from $93.69 last session and now $14.09 above the $80 FY27 line — a sustained push through $90.
chart_read.implication: Treasury: each dollar on Brent re-widens the import bill and the FY27 subsidy claim — the $90 break holds, watch $95.

sections.verdict: Remittance held $2.82bn — a second month under $3bn as oil bites.
sections.analysis: Remittance is the earned-dollar engine that has to cover the gap the trade account cannot, and it is losing altitude. July printed $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn — and the margin it clears over the $1.77bn trade gap has stopped growing at roughly $1.05bn. The other side of the runway is widening: Brent has pressed to $94.09, $14.09 above the $80 FY27 line, lifting the import bill soft demand had masked. And the buffer behind both is stale — reserves last printed $36.42bn on 31 Jul, cover 6.28mo, the August refresh three weeks overdue. Neither engine is broken; exports hold $4.03bn, the taka is firm at 122.07. But the trajectory has turned: inflows flat, the oil bill rising, the reserve check unpaid. The book stays defensive on the peg — long reserve visibility, reading a firm taka as demand weakness, not dollar strength.

banker_read.verdict: July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while the buffer stopped rebuilding: reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo. Both earned-dollar engines are soft, exports at $4.03bn, and Brent's push to $94.09 now pulls the other way.
